extracted.intended_audience: media scholars, political communication researchers, and newsroom editors interested in partisan selective exposure and newsworthiness
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing or modelling which stories are newsworthy for particular outlets by accounting for audience partisan predispositions and selective exposure dynamics. Useful for researchers building measures of newsworthiness, and editors/analysts examining placement and engagement patterns across partisan media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong Selective Exposure Effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Conservatives consume conservative-leaning outlets; liberals consume liberal-leaning outlets, beyond what topic interest alone explains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical finding from 2004 National Annenberg Election Survey data showing partisanship predicts consumption of newspapers, talk radio, cable TV news, and Internet news; implies audience political predispositions are a primary driver of media selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect Strongest in High-Choice Media
rubrics_metrics.description: Selective exposure is stronger in media environments with more choice (cable TV and Internet) than in lower-choice media like newspapers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When modelling or predicting audience behavior or news placement, weight choice-rich platforms as amplifiers of partisan sorting; greater outlet and channel choice increases the magnitude of partisan selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Talk Radio Most Polarized
rubrics_metrics.description: Talk radio exhibits the highest selective exposure of any medium tested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat talk radio as an extreme case of audience partisan homogeneity and use it as a benchmark when comparing polarization across media platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cumulative Across Media
rubrics_metrics.description: People who selectively expose in one medium tend to do so across all media — partisan media diet is consistent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for cross-media consumption patterns (users who seek partisan-consistent content in one channel are likely to do so elsewhere); multi-platform measures of audience partisanship improve predictive validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience-Targeted Selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Outlets tailor selection to their partisan audience; what's newsworthy on Fox News differs from what's newsworthy on MSNBC even controlling for editorial values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model newsworthiness at the outlet-audience level rather than assuming a universal newsworthiness score; editorial selection is informed by anticipated audience reactions and partisan compatibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partisan-Salience Premium
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories that resonate with the outlet's partisan audience receive better placement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating placement or prominence, include a 'salience-to-audience' factor — content aligning with audience priorities should predict higher placement and prominence metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outgroup-Negativity Bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories framing the political outgroup negatively perform better than stories framing them positively, on partisan-leaning outlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coding frames for valence toward political outgroups is important; expect and measure a positive effect of outgroup-negative framing on placement, prominence, and engagement on partisan outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirmation Premium
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories that confirm the audience's worldview earn higher engagement and therefore better placement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include measures of congruence between story assertions and audience priors; congruent content should predict engagement-driven amplification and editorial promotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Belief-Dissonance Penalty
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories that challenge audience priors are demoted unless they can be reframed (e.g., as 'elite hypocrisy').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When encountering dissonant facts, check for reframing strategies; outlets may still run challenging stories but will temper or reframe them to reduce audience dissonance and preserve placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-screening for Compatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors anticipate audience reaction and pre-screen stories for partisan compatibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In newsroom workflows and content selection models, include a pre-selection filter that predicts audience compatibility and likely editorial acceptance; use historical audience reactions to parameterize the filter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differential Framing of Same Events
rubrics_metrics.description: The same wire story gets different headlines and emphasis in different outlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When comparing coverage across outlets, analyze headline selection, lede emphasis, and framing differences; identical events should be coded for differences in emphasis and interpretive frames rather than treated as the same story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differential Weighting of Source Perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Some outlets foreground sympathetic sources, others foreground critical ones, on the same event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code source selection and prominence (which voices are quoted, whose perspectives are centered) as a mechanism of partisan selection; source weighting affects perceived newsworthiness for each audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic Agenda Differentiation
rubrics_metrics.description: Beyond framing, outlets differ in which topics they cover at all (e.g., Hunter Biden coverage vs. Trump coverage volume varies markedly).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure topic-level coverage frequency across outlets — topic selection itself is a partisan signal and a key determinant of what is treated as newsworthy by different audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement-Driven Amplification
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories that generate selective-exposure-friendly engagement are pushed harder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating placement and prominence, incorporate engagement metrics as both outcome and causal mechanism — high engagement from partisan audiences feeds back into editorial promotion and algorithmic amplification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filter-Bubble / Echo-Chamber Connection
rubrics_metrics.description: Selective exposure existed before algorithmic personalization; algorithms amplify a pre-existing audience tendency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In analyses of algorithmic effects, treat individual selective exposure as a baseline; evaluate amplification effects relative to this pre-existing audience sorting rather than assuming emergence solely from personalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outlet Segmentation as a Measurable Variable
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsworthiness varies by outlet partisan profile; homogeneous newsworthiness scores across outlets are misspecified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operationalize outlet-level partisan scores (e.g., AllSides, Media Bias/Fact Check) and incorporate them into models of story selection and placement instead of using one-size-fits-all newsworthiness measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operationalizable Measurement Strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Outlet-level partisan scores can be combined with story content to test partisan-selection patterns at scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use existing partisan-leaning labels/scores and automated content measures to create scalable tests of selective exposure and partisan newsworthiness; this enables empirical testing of placement, framing, and engagement hypotheses across many outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Front-Page Placement Is Partisan-Encoded
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors implicitly select for partisan-friendly stories even at outlets that disclaim partisan orientation; front-page placement reflects partisan encoding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analyzing homepage/front-page prominence, treat placement as an editorial signal shaped by anticipated audience partisan preferences; do not assume neutral gatekeeping even in outlets that claim neutrality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience Metrics Amplify Selective Exposure
rubrics_metrics.description: When metric-driven outlets cater to existing audience, they reinforce selective-exposure patterns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how metrics-driven decision-making (clicks, shares, time-on-page) interacts with audience partisanship: outlets optimizing for these metrics will disproportionately promote content that fits partisan audience preferences, reinforcing selective exposure.
